market_mood: Geopolitics still dominates: stalled US-Iran talks, Houthi attacks near Saudi airspace and a US pullout from Iraq are keeping oil above $90, while a cooler-than-expected PCE print supported stocks and a heavy wave of M&A clearances (Skyworks/Qorvo, Integer/KKR) kept deal desks busy. Micron's earnings after the close is the key tech catalyst.
self_check: My record is mixed (45%), with merger-arb ideas the weakest (1 of 5) and oil and rate calls the best, so today I leaned toward energy and kept deal plays small and only where regulatory approval is already in hand.

picks.reason: Oil is above $91 with US-Iran talks stalled, Houthi attacks prompting a Saudi airspace advisory and the US strategic reserve at 44-year lows, which keeps a geopolitical premium in crude.
Skyworks said it has received all regulatory clearances for the Qorvo combination, removing the main hurdle and narrowing the deal spread as closing approaches.
Jet fuel costs rise with crude above $91 and tight diesel/distillate markets, plus Middle East airspace advisories complicate routes ahead of Delta's October 9 earnings.

Integer received early termination of the antitrust waiting period for its pending acquisition by KKR, speeding the path to closing.
Caterpillar announced a $1 billion North Carolina expansion and agreed to buy the Fabick dealership, signals of confidence in demand and more control over distribution.

watchlist_notes.note: Cooler-than-expected August PCE lifted the major indexes, but high oil and Iran risk cap the upside.
Nasdaq led Wednesday's gains and Micron's results after the bell are the next swing factor for chip-heavy exposure.
The Dow rose on the inflation surprise; no Dow-specific news today.
No major company news today beyond general Dow index moves.
Commentary on Azure backlog and Copilot growth remains bullish, though heavy AI capex versus free cash flow is the main worry.
No fresh company news, but Micron's memory results tonight will set the tone for AI chip sentiment.
Rosenblatt raised its target to $360 and argued AI shopping agents won't break Amazon's retail media model.
Alphabet joined other AI firms in signing a White House accord; no other direct news.
Stock has rallied hard on AI hopes, but analysts are split as free cash flow shrinks under $130B+ of AI spending.
Cathie Wood added shares while a bear flagged roughly $30 billion of future cash needs from AI and factory spending.
Active in big lending and a new Ford manufacturing finance platform; a cooler inflation print is mildly supportive for credit.
Crude above $91 with the SPR at 44-year lows and Iran talks stalled is a clear tailwind for the integrated majors.
Gold stays supported by Iran tensions, though the cooler inflation reading trims the panic bid.

top_buys.pitch: Crude above $91 with a stalled Iran deal and an emptied strategic reserve keeps the majors' cash flow strong.
top_buys.why: US-Iran talks have stalled and Washington is pulling forces out of Iraq, while Houthi attacks triggered an EU airspace advisory over Saudi Arabia. The US strategic petroleum reserve sits at 44-year lows, so there is little cushion if supply is disrupted. Integrated majors like Exxon convert higher crude and tight diesel cracks directly into cash flow.
top_buys.risks: A sudden diplomatic breakthrough with Iran, or demand worries, could knock $5-10 off crude and take energy shares with it.
top_buys.watch: Headlines on the seven-day US-Iran trust-building plan and weekly US crude inventory data.

top_buys.pitch: All regulatory clearances are in hand for the Skyworks combination, so the remaining deal risk is small.
top_buys.why: Skyworks confirmed it has every necessary approval and expects to close the merger soon. When the antitrust overhang lifts, target shares usually drift toward the deal value. That gives a fairly defined, event-driven setup rather than a bet on the chip cycle.
top_buys.risks: Merger-arb spreads are thin, so the upside is limited, and any late financing or closing hiccup could hit the stock hard.
top_buys.watch: The formal closing announcement and the exchange ratio terms.

top_buys.pitch: A $1B US expansion and a dealership buyout signal management confidence in sustained demand.
top_buys.why: Caterpillar is putting $1 billion into North Carolina capacity and buying the Fabick dealership, which adds margin from distribution. Big capital commitments like this usually come when order books are healthy, including data-center and power-related equipment demand. Cooler inflation also eases the rate pressure on industrial capex.
top_buys.risks: Industrials are cyclical and a slowdown or a spike in rates would quickly punish the multiple; the spending also raises near-term costs.
top_buys.watch: Caterpillar's next quarterly results and dealer inventory commentary.

top_buys.pitch: Early antitrust termination clears the path for KKR's buyout of this medical device CDMO.
top_buys.why: Integer received early termination of the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period, removing the biggest regulatory step. With a well-funded private equity buyer, the probability of completion rises and the shares should track toward the agreed price. It is a low-drama, low-return setup.
top_buys.risks: If the deal price is already fully reflected, there is almost no upside left, and any break would cause a large drop.
top_buys.watch: Shareholder vote timing and the expected closing date.

top_buys.pitch: New CEO Roger Lynch takes over just as holiday retail sales are forecast to top $1 trillion.
top_buys.why: Mattel replaced Ynon Kreiz with Roger Lynch as CEO and Chairman, a change that often brings fresh strategy and cost focus. The timing lines up with forecasts for record holiday retail spending. Expectations for the toy sector are low, so any decent holiday read could lift shares.
top_buys.risks: CEO changes create uncertainty and much of the holiday sales growth is just inflation, not real volume; tariffs on toys remain a cost risk.
top_buys.watch: Mattel's third-quarter results and any strategic commentary from the new CEO.
